acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Trolls family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Bog Troll, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Lodged-Blade Grapple Soldier (Soldier) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Thicker-limbed than a Scrag, with tumorous regrowth knots across the shoulders, wet bog hide, a rope coil, and a rusted blade still visibly lodged in the side.

Signature mechanic: Bog Anchor: the Troll hooks a rope around the blade in its side and throws the loop with one long arm; if the loop catches, it braces against tumorous shoulder knots and drags the target toward the blade-side wound.
battlefieldDuty: Apply repeatable pin pressure by using the rusted blade healed into its side as an anchor for a long-arm drag, then regenerate behind shoulder knots while the target is held.
constructionDimensions: Anatomy and materials remain physical bog flesh: rubbery hide, wet scar tissue, bark-hard callus, mud, rope, rags, embedded bone, and corroded weapons show ordinary decay and rapid biological repair.
Motion and surface effects remain bodily and local: muscle bunching, wound contraction, clear fluid, mud slough, scar cracking, and displaced breath reveal regeneration without magical residue.
counterplay: Avoid the widening rope loop, cut it during the drag, or strike the rusted blade sideways to reopen the anchor wound and soften the braced shoulder. Affinity signal: Open wound rims, pale regrowth buds, lodged-object anchors, scar seams, and forming head stalks preserve the exact physical interruption points described by each form.
forbiddenTreatments: Clean symmetrical healing that erases the family's accumulated wrongness
identityInvariants: Tall, stooped, potbellied humanoid silhouette with a small head on a thick neck and disproportionately long arms hanging past the knees.
Bog green, liver-brown, sallow grey, bruise purple, and wet glistening highlights keep living hide distinct from mud and scavenged rags.
Rubbery skin, scar tissue, bark-hard callus, mud, rope, and half-swallowed equipment remain visibly bodily rather than worn as deliberate finery.
Healed-over piercings, embedded bones, lodged weapons, misplaced limbs, stray jaws, and layered scars record prior injury as readable construction history.
Escalation adds accumulated misregrowth rather than simple size: open gashes become knots, alternate organs, defensive scar architecture, and finally a walking archive of incompatible healing.
telegraph: The shoulder knots harden, one hand feeds muddy rope around the protruding blade, and the potbelly turns so the blade-side gash faces the target.
